fix(deep-link): hit Funnelcake REST before relays for /video/<id> (#4177)

* fix(deep-link): hit Funnelcake REST before relays for /video/<id>

Cold-start `divine.video/video/<sha256>` deep-links were waiting 60s+
behind a generic spinner. Two compounding causes:

1. `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` ran three lookups in series: relay
   query by event id (always misses for Blossom-hashed share URLs)
   → relay query by d-tag → Funnelcake REST. `NostrClient.queryEvents`
   waits for EOSE from every relay in the pool with a 5s default
   timeout, and any relay still mid-connect during cold start blocks
   the whole batch. The on-relay-ready retry then re-runs the entire
   sequence, doubling the wait.

2. `VideoDetailScreen`'s loading state used a generic Material
   `CircularProgressIndicator` instead of the branded sprite-sheet
   indicator the rest of the app uses.

Reorder the route lookup to: local cache → Funnelcake REST → relay
queries (each capped by `_routeRelayTimeout = 3s`). REST answers in
<1s without waiting on relay connection state and is the canonical
source for divine.video share URLs; relay is kept as fallback for
events that only exist on user-configured personal relays. Swap the
spinner to BrandedLoadingIndicator.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(deep-link): bound stats hydration and narrow relay timeout per review

Addresses two blocking review comments on PR #4177:

1. The REST-first route helpers (`_fetchVideoFromRouteApi`,
   `_fetchRouteVideoFromLocalCache`, `_fetchRouteVideoByEventIdFromRelay`,
   `_fetchVideoByStableIdFromRelay`) now bound `_hydrateVideosWithBulkStats`
   with `_statsFetchTimeout` (3s, degrades to the unhydrated video on
   timeout). Without this, a stalled `getBulkVideoStats` would re-stall
   the deep-link spinner even after the route event itself had been
   fetched quickly — exactly the regression the original reorder set
   out to fix. Mirrors the existing pattern in `fetchVideoWithStats`.

2. The relay-only timeout now wraps each helper's `queryEvents` call
   itself, not the whole helper. Previously, a 3s outer wrap around
   `getVideosByAddressableIds` (which also runs Funnelcake fallback +
   stats hydration internally) could kill a successful relay result
   whose only slow step was downstream enrichment. Introduces
   `_fetchAddressableVideoFromRelay` for the relay-only addressable
   path so the orchestrator can call it without the broad pipeline
   wrap, and pushes `.timeout(_routeRelayTimeout, …)` down onto the
   `queryEvents` invocation in each of the three relay helpers.

Two new tests pin the contract: stats hang doesn't block REST route
resolution, and addressable relay success doesn't get killed when
stats hydration stalls.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(deep-link): align addressable relay path with sibling helpers (review)

Self-review nits on top of 765a29d:

- Document why _fetchAddressableVideoFromRelay deliberately drops the
  Funnelcake fallback that getVideosByAddressableIds did: the orchestrator
  already runs Funnelcake REST as step 2 with funnelcakeRouteId =
  candidate.stableId ?? candidate.eventId, and _VideoRouteCandidate.parse
  populates stableId from decoded.id / aid.dTag for both naddr and raw
  `kind:pubkey:d-tag` inputs, so REST has already been attempted. The
  pre-fix duplicate fallback was redundant in this code path.

- Relax the addressable kind gate from NIP71VideoKinds.isVideoKind
  (strict 34236-only) to NIP71VideoKinds.isAcceptableVideoKind (21 / 22 /
  34235 / 34236) for parity with _fetchRouteVideoByEventIdFromRelay and
  _fetchVideoByStableIdFromRelay. The pre-existing strict-only behavior
  was inherited from getVideosByAddressableIds and meant a naddr1 link
  pointing at a legacy NIP-71 short video would silently miss in the
  addressable branch even though the same content resolves via raw event
  id or bare d-tag.

New regression test pins the new behavior: naddr1 / kind 22 resolves
through the addressable relay branch instead of dropping at the kind gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
chore: remove FFmpeg residue from Android, iOS, and tests (#4166)

FFmpeg-kit was removed from the app some time ago (no Dart imports, no
pubspec entry), but defensive shims and stale comments remained in
build configs and one test fixture. This sweep clears them out:

- codemagic.yaml: drop the `xcode: 16.1` pin (and its FFmpeg-Kit linker
  comment) on the two iOS workflows that still carried it. Remaining
  iOS workflows already use `xcode: latest`; this aligns the rest.
- mobile/android/app/build.gradle.kts: drop the three
  `com.arthenica.ffmpegkit` excludes from `configurations.all` and the
  trailing `// Exclude FFmpeg native libraries…` comment. Update the
  libc++_shared.so packaging comment to reflect that c2pa-android is
  the only remaining duplicate-shared-lib source.
- mobile/android/app/src/main/kotlin/co/openvine/app/MainActivity.kt:
  remove the try/catch that swallowed `FFmpegKit`-named init failures
  around `super.configureFlutterEngine`. With the plugin gone, the
  branch was dead code that masked any real engine-init exception.
- mobile/test/services/audio_extraction_service_test.dart: replace the
  `'FFmpeg failed'` test fixture string with `'Audio extraction
  failed'`. The literal is arbitrary — the assertion is on
  `AudioExtractionException.toString()` echoing whatever message it
  was constructed with — but the old value implied a backend that no
  longer exists.

commit.message:
feat(dm): self-wrap-only recovery for sentPartial sends (#4106)

* feat(dm): self-wrap-only recovery for sentPartial sends

Closes #4102.

Tapping Retry on the sentPartial SnackBar previously redispatched the
full ConversationMessageSent path, which republished the recipient
gift wrap and double-delivered the message. NIP-17 self-wraps are
independent of recipient wraps — only the missing self-wrap needs to
land on retry, never the recipient one.

- NIP17MessageService.publishSelfWrap: builds + publishes only the
  sender self-addressed gift wrap for a pre-existing rumor, sharing
  the self-wrap helper with sendRumor.
- DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap(rumorId): looks up the queue row,
  rebuilds the rumor from its rumor_event_json (preserving the
  receiver-side dedup key), publishes via publishSelfWrap, then
  deletes the row on success or marks self_wrap_status failed for the
  retry sweep. Idempotent against an already-sent row, defends
  against missing rows, foreign-owner rows, and a missing queue DAO.
- DmRepository.sendGroupMessage: refactored to enqueue a queue row
  per recipient (mirroring sendMessage) and to write per-recipient
  outcomes inside the same transaction as the local message persist.
  This is what lets group recovery scope to only the affected
  successful recipient sends.
- ConversationState: PartialSend(rumorIds) carries the per-recipient
  rumor ids whose self-wrap failed; lastPartialSend lives alongside
  lastFailedSend with its own clear flag in copyWith. The two states
  drive different recovery paths, so they're tracked independently.
- ConversationBloc: on sentPartial, populates lastPartialSend (not
  lastFailedSend) with the rumor ids of the partial-self results.
  New ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested event with sequential
  transformer; the handler loops recoverSelfWrap per id, aggregates
  outcomes, and reduces lastPartialSend.rumorIds to only the
  still-failing ids so a second Retry tap targets exactly those.
- ConversationView: the SnackBar Retry callback branches on
  sendStatus — sentPartial dispatches the recovery event, failed
  keeps dispatching ConversationMessageSent.

Tests pin the no-duplicate-recipient-publish contract: the recovery
path goes through dmRepository.recoverSelfWrap and never touches
sendMessage / sendGroupMessage.

* refactor(dm): close self-wrap recovery duplicate-publish hole

Address review feedback on PR #4106:

- recoverSelfWrap success path now falls back to
  markSelfWrapStatus(sent, eventId) when deleteById throws, so the
  next sweep short-circuits via the idempotent already-sent guard
  instead of republishing the self-wrap. Both writes failing remains
  safe (NIP-17 receive-side dedup), surfaced via logs.
- Extract the recipient-success / self-wrap-failed queue transition
  shared by sendMessage and sendGroupMessage into
  _finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess so the two paths can't drift.
- Tighten the idempotent-guard comment to describe the post-fix
  reachable path (concurrent recovery OR fallback-marked row).

Tests: two new recoverSelfWrap scenarios pin the deleteById-throws
fallback and the doubly-degraded "both writes throw" path. Existing
sendMessage / sendGroupMessage queue tests are unchanged - they
assert at the DAO-call surface, which is invariant under the helper
extraction.

* test(dm): remove recovery bookkeeping debt

---------

Co-authored-by: Liz Sweigart <127434495+NotThatKindOfDrLiz@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
fix(video): preserve like counts and engagement tags after metadata edit (#4150)

* fix(video): preserve like counts and engagement tags after metadata edit

After a user edited their video (e.g. changing hashtags), two bugs caused
engagement counts to drop to zero:

1. _mergeUpdatedVideo (previously _preserveOriginalTimestamp) now carries
   nostrLikeCount forward from the existing video when the incoming update
   has null — which is always the case after VideoEvent.fromNostrEvent(),
   since that field is runtime-injected and never stored in Nostr tags.
   The relay-fetched count will overwrite it once the next batch fires,
   so there is no risk of a stale count persisting.

2. _updateVideo() in share_video_menu now re-adds loops/likes/reposts/views
   tags from the original nostrEventTags when rebuilding the replacement
   event. These tags are baked into Vine-imported video events and were
   being silently dropped on every edit, permanently zeroing originalLoops
   and originalLikes.

Also renames _preserveOriginalTimestamp to _mergeUpdatedVideo to reflect
the broader responsibility of the function.

* test(share_video_menu): exercise production engagement-tag filter

Addresses review on PR #4150: the previous tests defined a standalone
_extractEngagementTags helper at the bottom of the test file that was
a verbatim copy of the production filter inside _updateVideo. Tests
asserted the helper's behaviour, not the production code's, so a
regression in _updateVideo would not have been caught.

Extract the filter to a top-level extractEngagementCountTags function
in share_video_menu.dart, gated on @visibleForTesting, and have both
production (_updateVideo) and tests call it. Also drops the redundant
tag.isNotEmpty check since tag.length >= 2 already implies non-empty.

fix(profile-editor): block save while avatar upload is in flight

Reviewer on PR #3916 flagged a residual race in the staged-avatar
model: Save remained enabled during the upload window, and
`_resolveEffectivePicture` would fall back to `persistedPictureUrl`
in that gap — publishing kind 0 with the OLD picture and forcing the
user to Save again once the staged URL landed.

Close it in both layers:

- `ProfileEditorState.isSaveReady` returns false while
  `pendingAvatarStatus == uploading`. `_SaveButton` reads this via
  `canSave`, so the UI gate falls out automatically.
- `ProfileEditorBloc._onProfileSaved` early-returns with a `Log.info`
  if a save event slips past the UI gate (retry CTAs, future
  callers). Belt-and-braces, not redundant — the publish path can't
  race the staged URL even if the UI invariant breaks later.

Tests added in `profile_editor_bloc_test.dart`:
- `isSaveReady returns false while an avatar upload is in flight`
- `isSaveReady returns true once the upload settles to staged`
  (sanity check that the gate is `uploading`, not "any non-idle")
- `ProfileSaved while uploading is dropped — no publish, no claim`
  asserts no state emission and `verifyNever` on `saveProfileEvent`,
  `claimUsername`, and `getCachedProfile`.

fix(l10n): replace profileSetupUploadSuccess with staged-state copy

Previous key "Profile picture uploaded successfully!" overstated what
happened when the upload finished — Save still has to publish, so users
saw the success-toned snackbar while the on-screen avatar still rendered
the old kind-0. The reviewer specifically called this out as confusing
copy.

Replace with profileSetupUploadStaged: "Uploaded — tap Save to apply"
in en.arb (with description metadata) and translate across all 16 other
locales. The old key wasn't referenced from any Dart code (was added
ahead of the migration that this PR completes), so removing it is safe.

Regenerated app_localizations.dart via `flutter gen-l10n`.

refactor(profile-setup): read avatar from bloc, drop widget-local state

Widget previously held its own _isUploadingImage / _uploadedImageUrl /
_selectedImageFilename and ran the upload inline in _uploadSelectedImage.
That left two sources of truth (widget local + ProfileSaved.picture) and
forced Save to look at widget state, which is why the post-upload
snackbar lied about being "applied" while the avatar widget rendered the
old kind-0.

Switch the screen to read pendingAvatarStatus + effectivePictureUrl from
ProfileEditorBloc. _pickImage dispatches ProfilePictureUploadRequested
(file or bytes flavor); the manual-URL sheet dispatches
ProfilePictureUrlSet on close. A new BlocListener fires the staged
snackbar on `uploading -> staged` and the localized failure snackbar on
`uploading -> failed` (mapped from the bloc's AvatarUploadError enum,
not raw exception text).

The BlocProvider key is composed from the captured Riverpod deps tuple
(profileRepository, blossomUploadService, pubkey) per
state_management.md, so a runtime auth flip rebuilds the bloc with
fresh dependencies instead of silently keeping the captured chain.

feat(profile-editor): stage avatar uploads in bloc state

Reviewer asked for a "dirty form" model on the profile edit screen: the
avatar should preview the new picture immediately after upload, but Save
remains the only path that publishes a kind-0 event. Web users were
seeing a confusing "uploaded successfully" snackbar while the avatar
still rendered the old picture (#3862, #3916 review).

Move ownership of the staged-avatar contract into ProfileEditorBloc so
the UI can stay thin: state distinguishes idle / uploading / staged /
failed, and exposes `effectivePictureUrl = pendingPictureUrl ??
persistedPictureUrl`. Failure preserves any prior staged URL — a failed
retry must not blank a previously-staged preview. AvatarUploadError
classifies the failure at the catch site so the UI maps an enum to a
localized snackbar instead of state carrying error strings (per
error_handling.md).

Save reads the effective picture from state, so the same publish path
works whether the user uploaded, pasted a URL, or kept the existing
avatar. Concurrent picks are dropped (droppable transformer) so a
second pick while uploading doesn't race the first.

fix(profile): drop dead stripMetadataWeb path; log unreachable upload guard

Per @hm21's review on #3916: `stripMetadataWeb` reads `dart:io File` from
its `inputPath`, which throws on web against `image_picker`'s blob URL —
so the `kIsWeb` branch in `stripMetadata` never actually worked on web for
the avatar flow. The PR's `stripMetadataBytes` is the correct web path,
making `stripMetadataWeb` dead code. Delete it and its test group, mark
the path-based APIs native-only in the docstring, and route web callers
to `stripMetadataBytes`.

Also log when `_uploadSelectedImage` is reached with neither file nor
bytes set — a programming error that the bare early-return was hiding.

fix(blossom-upload): cover bytes path to keep CI strict-coverage gate green

The strict-coverage gate (`min_coverage: 100`) flagged 8 lines added
in #3916: a dead `_UploadSource.size` getter (never called — internal
helpers track `fileSize` separately) and the outer `on Object catch`
in `uploadImageBytes`.

- Remove the unused `size` getter and the orphaned `fileSize` field
  on `_FileUploadSource`. All four callers already passed `fileSize`
  as a separate parameter, so the constructor argument was redundant.
- Add a single-caller-per-source contract note to `_UploadSource.readRange`
  to make the implicit serialization requirement (the file impl mutates
  a shared `RandomAccessFile` position) explicit.
- Add a test that drives the `uploadImageBytes` outer catch by making
  `authProvider.isAuthenticated` throw, mirroring the existing
  `uploadImage returns failure when file processing throws` test.
- Relax the brittle `progress.first / progress.last` assertion in the
  legacy-PUT bytes test to `contains(0.1) / contains(1.0)` so adding
  intermediate progress milestones won't break the test.

fix(profile): wire avatar upload through bytes API on web (#3887)

Avatar upload was a no-op on web. `image_picker` returns a blob URL
that `dart:io File` cannot resolve, so every read in
`stripMetadataInPlace` and `BlossomUploadService.uploadImage` threw at
the first I/O call. PR #3880's friendlier error classifier hid the
exception behind the generic fallback snackbar. The desktop picker
branch was equally broken because `defaultTargetPlatform` reports the
host OS in a desktop browser.

Fix:

- `BlossomUploadService` gains `uploadImageBytes(bytes, filename, ...)`
  for the web path. The internal upload helpers now route through a
  `_UploadSource` abstraction so the file (streaming) and bytes
  (in-memory) paths share the same Blossom BUD-01 plumbing,
  including resumable chunked uploads. `uploadImage(File)` is
  unchanged so native callers still get the platform-channel EXIF
  stripper.
- `ImageMetadataStripper` gains `stripMetadataBytes` — pure-Dart EXIF
  removal that mirrors `stripMetadataInPlace`'s rename rule (PNG keeps
  its extension; everything else re-encodes to JPEG).
- `profile_setup_screen` picks an `XFile`, reads the bytes on web, and
  uploads via `uploadImageBytes`. Native picks keep the `dart:io File`
  flow. `_isDesktopPlatform()` now returns `false` on web so a
  Mac/Linux browser stops routing through `file_selector`.

fix(notifications): clear unread badge by syncing Riverpod cache on inbox open (#4165)

* fix(notifications): clear unread badge by syncing Riverpod cache on inbox open

Closes #4144 (duplicate of #4048). Supersedes #4149 by addressing all
three CHANGES_REQUESTED blockers:

1) NotificationFeedMarkAllRead fired from initState before _onStarted
   finished its async fetch, so the early-exit guard in _onMarkAllRead
   saw the empty initial state and returned without calling
   markAllAsRead. Re-dispatch the existing event from _onStarted's
   success branch instead of inlining a weaker mark-read variant —
   preserves the rollback / addError path added by #4034.

2) The bottom-nav badge and inbox segmented-toggle count are driven by
   relayNotificationsProvider (legacy Riverpod), but the BLoC-driven
   inbox never updated that cache, so the badge stayed unread until
   the 5-min auto-refresh fired. Centralize the Riverpod sync at the
   page-wrapper level (InboxNotificationsPage scaffold and standalone
   NotificationsPage), guarded by an unread check, so it fires once
   per open instead of fanning out across the five NotificationsView
   tab instances mounted by TabBarView.

3) Use ref.listenManual with fireImmediately:true so the sync covers
   both warm-cache opens (provider already loaded by the bottom nav)
   and cold-start opens (still resolving when the page mounts) without
   firing a no-op API write when there is nothing unread.

Tests:
- BLoC: assert markAllAsRead is called once after NotificationFeedStarted
  with unread items, and verifyNever when the loaded page is already
  all-read. Update the existing isFollowingBack-derivation test to
  expect the new third state from the optimistic mark-all-read flip.
- New inbox_notifications_page_test.dart: verify markAllAsRead fires
  exactly once on inbox open, never on all-read, and stays at one call
  after swiping through all five filter tabs.
- Extend notifications_page_test.dart with the same assertions for the
  standalone /notifications/:index route.

* docs(notifications): rephrase brainstorm to avoid lazy-stub classifier

The brainstorm doc referenced the existing `notifications-refactor`
deferred-removal comment in `relay_notifications_provider.dart:1` by
quoting its literal text, which the divine-brain `lazy-stub` classifier
flagged as a new unfinished-work marker (#4165 review). Rephrase the
references to describe the marker without quoting it verbatim — the
existing marker remains in code untouched, only the doc text changes.

* docs(notifications): convert badge-desync brainstorm to decision record

Address the remaining CHANGES_REQUESTED item on #4165: the brainstorm
doc still read as a planning artifact after Approach A landed. Reframe
"Recommendation" as a past-tense "Decision" that explicitly links #3596
(Delete dual notification system) as the tracker for Approach C, and
drop "Open Questions for /plan", "Prerequisites", and "Next Step" —
Approach A's open questions are answered by what shipped; Approach C's
questions belong in #3596. Adds a brief "Outcome" section at the bottom
linking the shipped files and the follow-up issue.

No code changes. Constraints, Prior Art, and Approaches Explored remain
intact so the rationale for rejecting B / D is preserved as historical
context for the next person picking up #3596.

Existing tests jump in at the `onAttestedEventHandlerReady` seam, so

EventChannel → Dart` path has no coverage. A loopback HTTP fixture
with a same-origin iframe drives the real WKWebView and asserts

fix(support): save logs to Downloads on desktop instead of share sheet (#4143)

* fix(support): save logs to Downloads on desktop instead of share sheet

share_plus on macOS/Windows/Linux requires a sharePositionOrigin
anchor frame the support screen can't supply, so the share popover
fails silently and the user sees "Failed to export logs". Desktop
users want the file written to disk anyway so they can attach it
manually.

Branch the export flow on platform: desktop writes the log file
directly to ~/Downloads via path_provider's getDownloadsDirectory and
the support screen shows a snackbar with the saved path plus a
"Show in folder" action that opens Finder/Explorer. Mobile keeps the
existing share sheet behaviour; web keeps the browser-download path.
The macOS Downloads entitlement is already set so no native plumbing
changes are needed.

and can pick where the log file lands. Downloads is still the

Add a cancelled state to LogExportResult so the UI can stay silent

commit.message:
fix(share): always emit https URL, never nostr:nevent (#4151)

Sharing a video sometimes produced `nostr:nevent1...` instead of an
`https://divine.video/...` URL because the share builders gated the web
URL on the presence of `rawTags['d']` and fell back to a NIP-19 nevent
otherwise.

The gate is dead weight:
- `VideoEvent.stableId` already returns `vineId ?? id`, and `vineId`
  itself falls back to the event ID when no `d` tag is present
  (`video_event.dart:589-595`).
- The `/video/:id` route handler accepts raw event IDs, d-tags, and
  NIP-19 references (`video_detail_screen.dart:41-42`).

So `https://divine.video/video/${video.stableId}` is always routable.
Drop the gate and the nostr-URI fallback in both `share_service.dart`
and `video_sharing_service.dart`. Users that explicitly want a Nostr
link still get one via `generateNostrEventLink` / "Copy Nostr link" in
the share bottom sheet.

* docs: add build-speed onboarding and cache reset guidance

so the targeted run_dev workflows referenced in docs/BUILD_SPEED_CHECKLIST.md

Eliminates the "Resolving dependencies / Downloading packages" pass that
ran twice on every build: once explicitly, once from `dart run
build_runner`. The scripts now (1) hash pubspec.yaml + pubspec.lock and
skip pub get when the hash matches a marker in .dart_tool/, and (2)
short-circuit the standalone pub get when codegen is in effect since
build_runner does its own resolve.

Net effect on a no-op rebuild: zero pub get cycles instead of two.

build_native.sh is gutted from a 190-line monolith into a thin dispatcher
that delegates to mobile/build_ios.sh and mobile/build_macos.sh, so all
platform-specific logic lives in one place. Closes the loop on the script
refactor referenced from docs/BUILD_SPEED_CHECKLIST.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

   the expensive cold-analyzer re-run.

short test-speed note (`--concurrency`, `--reporter=compact`, scoped
paths via `watch_tests.sh`).

commit.message:
fix(notifications): wire "liked your comment" + "replied" notification taps (#4130)

* fix(notifications): wire likeComment tap to navigate to comment thread

Tapping "X liked your comment" was a no-op because the ActorNotification
case for `likeComment` fell into a `break` that mistakenly assumed
likeComment wasn't actor-anchored — even though the model's assert says
it is.

Carry referencedEventId (the kind 1111 comment) as targetEventId on
ActorNotification, then route likeComment taps through the existing
NotificationTargetResolver path so the comment's `E` tag walks to the
parent video and the screen opens with the comments thread auto-opened.

Falls back to the actor's profile when targetEventId is missing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(notifications): stop rendering replies as "You have a new update"

Reply notifications (kind 1111 with notification_type 'reply') were
being silently coerced to NotificationKind.system in the repository's
actor-enrichment path because ActorNotification didn't accept reply.
That coercion produced a "You have a new update" row with the reply
text underneath, no actor name, and no tap handler.

Split the reply path the same way reactions are split:
- 'reply' on a video → NotificationKind.comment (groups under the
  existing video-anchored comment path; the user already understands
  this as a comment on their video).
- 'reply' on a non-video (i.e. a reply to one of the user's own
  comments) → NotificationKind.reply on an ActorNotification, with
  targetEventId carrying the parent. Tap routes through the same
  resolver path as likeComment to open the parent video with the
  comments thread auto-opened.

Adds NotificationKind.reply to ActorNotification's accept-list,
renders the row using the existing notificationRepliedToYourComment
ARB key, and reuses the kind-1111 E-tag resolver.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(profile): show divine.video handles as @user (no domain suffix) (#4131)

Adds UserProfile.shortDisplayNip05 — strips `.divine.video` /
`openvine.co` for divine-owned subdomains so users render as `@rabble`

is on the default divine domain. Short form matches Telegram/Fragment
behaviour and reads cleaner in feeds, mentions, and search.

intentionally keep the long form — those are surfaces where "what
domain do I own" is the actual answer the user is looking for.

search user tile, user profile tile, conversation view, message
request preview, welcome screen account block, find-people sheet,
user-picker sheet, clickable hashtag/mention text. The handle getter
on UserProfile now uses shortDisplayNip05, so any caller going through
.handle inherits the short form for free.

feat(router): add /explore/tab/:name URL for direct tab landing (#3899)

* feat(router): add /explore/tab/:name URL for direct tab landing

Adds a real, deep-linkable URL for selecting a specific tab inside
the Explore screen, replacing the previous force-provider redirect
trick for the empty-following landing.

- ExploreScreen.pathTabSubpath = '/explore/tab/:name'

commit.message:
fix(security): iOS per-frame origin attestation for Nostr bridge (#3979)

* hardening(apps): iOS per-frame origin attestation for Nostr bridge (#3764)

The pigeon layer in webview_flutter_wkwebview 3.24.1 truncates
WKScriptMessage to name+body only; frameInfo is not plumbed to Dart.
This introduces a native Swift plugin that uses the package's public
external API (FWFWebViewFlutterWKWebViewExternalAPI) to look up the
WKWebView and replace the pigeon-managed WKScriptMessageHandler with a
FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler that reads frameInfo.isMainFrame and
securityOrigin at the platform level.

The Dart sandbox screen activates attestation after addJavaScriptChannel
(which installs the JS alias window.divineSandboxBridge) and before the
first page load. On iOS, messages now arrive via EventChannel carrying
{message, isMainFrame, host, port, scheme}; _handleAttestedEvent rejects
any non-main-frame message with subframe_rejected before the nonce check
fires. Android is unchanged — nonce gate remains the effective defence
there; WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener is a follow-up.

Note: NostrBridgeAttestationPlugin.swift must be added to the Xcode
Runner target before building.

* chore(ios): add NostrBridgeAttestationPlugin.swift to Runner target

Adds the four required pbxproj entries (PBXBuildFile, PBXFileReference,
group child, Sources build phase) so the file compiles without a manual
Xcode step.

* fix(security): tighten iOS frame attestation per review feedback

- Single-instance enforcement: extract `NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy`
  state machine. Refuse a second `attach` with `ALREADY_ATTACHED`
  instead of silently overwriting the active eventSink — the previous
  shape was structurally broken under multiple sandbox WebViews.
- Observability: add `NSLog` on every native failure path
  (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `WEBVIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `ALREADY_ATTACHED`) and a
  `Log.warning` on the Dart side when `PlatformException` trips the
  nonce-only fallback. The degraded posture is now visible in unified
  logs instead of silent.
- Drop `host` / `port` / `scheme` from the native event payload —
  Dart only consumes `message` + `isMainFrame`. Updated the Dart tests
  that simulated those keys to match the actual native contract.
- Move the document-start `WKUserScript` installation into the Swift
  plugin (new `bootstrapScript` arg on `attach`). Removes the
  `package:webview_flutter_wkwebview/src/common/web_kit.g.dart`
  private-path import, eliminating the Dart layer's only crossing of
  that boundary.
- Add native unit tests at `RunnerTests/RunnerTests.swift` covering
  the policy state machine (initial state, idempotent re-attach,
  cross-id refusal, detach semantics, re-attach after detach), the
  `eventPayload` dictionary shape (security-relevant key set, no
  origin-field leakage), and the `WKUserContentController` lifecycle
  the plugin depends on.

* fix(security): address review feedback on iOS frame attestation

- Switch the native-attestation fallback warning from LogCategory.auth to
  LogCategory.system: bridge-attestation availability is a platform/system
  channel concern, not an authentication flow.
- Move group-scoped mutable state (attestedEventHandler, capturedScripts)
  in the iOS frame attestation tests into an explicit setUp block, so each
  case starts from a known state without an implicit reset hidden inside
  pumpSandbox.

* fix(security): narrow subframe id-extraction catch to FormatException

The best-effort id-extraction block in `_handleAttestedEvent` previously
caught everything (`catch (_) {}`), which silently swallowed unrelated
invariant bugs (StateError, TypeError) on a security-relevant path.
Narrow the catch to `FormatException` (the only thing `jsonDecode`
throws here) and document the intent in the block body, matching the
existing `on FormatException` pattern used at five other jsonDecode
sites in `lib/`. No observable behaviour change; all 34 sandbox tests
pass unchanged. Addresses rabble's review nit.

* fix(security): log unexpected attestation event shape

---------

commit.message:
feat(db): add outgoing_dms Drift table + DAO for durable DM queue (#3911)

* feat(db): add outgoing_dms Drift table + DAO for durable DM queue

Step 2 of the #3909 stack — adds the persistence layer for the durable
outgoing-DM queue. Pure data layer; no behavior change yet.

NIP-17 sends are two independent kind-1059 publishes (recipient gift
wrap + self-addressed gift wrap). The new `outgoing_dms` table tracks
each row with two independent status columns so a partial delivery
(recipient ✓, self ✗) can be retried on the missing wrap only — never
double-deliver to the recipient.

Schema highlights:
- `id` is the rumor event id (PRIMARY KEY) — stable across retries
  because `rumor_event_json` stores the serialized rumor and retries
  re-wrap the same one (rumor.id is a hash of its fields, so re-mint
  would break receiver-side dedup).
- `recipient_wrap_status` and `self_wrap_status` are independent
  string-encoded enums (`pending` | `sent` | `failed`). String form
  lets us add new states (e.g. `cancelled`) without a schema bump.
- `retry_count`, `last_error`, `last_attempt_at` mirror PendingActions
  for the retry service to drive backoff.
- `owner_pubkey` for multi-account isolation, mirroring
  `direct_messages.owner_pubkey`.
- Indexes for the access patterns the queue + retry service need:
  per-conversation watch, per-wrap-status retry sweeps, queued-at
  ordering.

fix(dm): surface NIP-17 self-wrap publish failure via NIP17SendResult (#3910)

* fix(dm): surface NIP-17 self-wrap publish failure via NIP17SendResult

NIP-17 sends two independent gift wraps to relays: one to the recipient
and one to the sender's own pubkey. The self-addressed wrap is what
makes the sender's own messages recoverable on reinstall, second-device
login, or fresh account state — without it, the recipient sees the
message but the sender does not on any other device.

`NIP17MessageService.sendPrivateMessage` published the recipient wrap,
then attempted the self-wrap inside a swallow-all `try { … } catch (e)
{ Log.error('Self-wrap failed (non-fatal): $e'); }`. That branch had
three failure paths — `getGiftWrapEvent` returned null, `publishEvent`
returned null, or the call threw — and the result type carried no
signal that any of them happened. Both `success: true with self-wrap
landed` and `success: true with self-wrap dropped` returned the same
`NIP17SendResult.success(...)`.

This is the F3 of the #3902 investigation. Without it, the durable
outgoing-message queue (#3909) cannot tell "fully delivered" from
"delivered to recipient only" and would either re-publish to the
recipient (double-deliver) or drop the row (sender's own history
silently rots).

- `NIP17SendResult` gains a `selfWrapPublished` field, defaulting to
  `true` so existing callers that don't yet care about per-wrap status
  are unaffected. Documented as only meaningful when `success: true`.
- `NIP17MessageService.sendPrivateMessage` now tracks the self-wrap
  outcome across all three failure paths and propagates it in the
  result. The catch still swallows (recipient was delivered) but logs
  with category-appropriate severity.
- New test pins the partial-delivery path: recipient-success +
  self-wrap-throws now returns `selfWrapPublished: false` (was
  unobservable before this change). Adds the "publishEvent returns
  null without throwing" case which was previously indistinguishable
  from the success path. Updates the prior test that pinned the
  swallow-all behavior — that was pinning the bug.
- Adds `nip17_send_result_test.dart` covering the success-default,
  explicit-false, and failure-branch field behavior.

Relates to #3909

* test(dm): cover self-wrap publish branches with valid sender pubkey

The self-wrap publish lines added in this PR (the inner publishEvent
call and its returns-null branch) were unreachable from the existing
test setup because the synthetic _testPublicKey is not a valid
secp256k1 point — the self-wrap's NIP-44 ECDH throws before the
publish call is reached, so coverage on the package dropped to
92.78% (gate is 93%).

Add a nested group that pairs LocalNostrSigner(_testPrivateKey)
with a sender pubkey actually derived via getPublicKey(), so the
self-wrap path runs end-to-end and we can drive both the
both-publishes-succeed branch and the self-wrap-publish-returns-null
branch from the mock relay client. Brings package coverage back to
93.04%.

* refactor(models): make NIP17SendResult.selfWrapPublished nullable

Address PR #3910 review (thread r3178622358): on the failure branch,
`selfWrapPublished` previously defaulted to `true`, exposing a concrete
success-like value on a result where the self-wrap is by definition
not attempted. With no production consumers downstream yet, this is
the right window to tighten the type before more callers depend on it.

- Field type changes from `bool` to `bool?`. The const constructor's
  default flips from `true` to `null`, so a direct `const NIP17SendResult(
  success: false, error: ...)` now produces `selfWrapPublished: null`
  rather than a misleading `true`.
- The `success(...)` factory keeps its `bool selfWrapPublished = true`
  parameter for backward compatibility with existing call sites that
  do not pass per-wrap status.
- The `failure(...)` factory keeps its current shape and lets the
  null default flow through — type encodes "not applicable on this
  branch."
- Class-level dartdoc reworded to drop the "(the DM outgoing-message
  queue) act on `selfWrapPublished` separately" forward reference;
  the queue (#3909) is not on `main` yet. Field dartdoc reworded to
  describe the surfaced state and to flag #3909 as the future home
  of retry handling without promising it as current behavior.
- Failure-branch model test updated: now asserts `selfWrapPublished
  is null` instead of pinning the soon-to-be-old `true` default.

No production consumers read `selfWrapPublished` outside this PR, so
no call-site migration is needed. Verified via `flutter analyze
packages/models packages/dm_repository lib test integration_test` and
the full `dm_repository` + `models` test suites.

Relates to #3909

* fix(dm): clarify self-wrap log copy and inject GiftWrapBuilder for tests

Addresses PR #3910 review threads r3178622356 (log/doc wording) and
r3178622359 (untested defensive null-event branch).

Wording (r3178622356): the prior block comment and three log lines
forward-referenced an "outgoing queue" that "will retry" the missing
self-wrap publish. That queue is the next PR in the #3909 stack and
is not on `main` yet, so the wording over-promised behavior that does
not exist. Reworded to describe the surfaced state ("recipient was
delivered, but the sender will not see this message on other devices
or after a reinstall") instead of asserting a future remediation. The
block comment retains a single `(see #3909)` breadcrumb framed as
"future retry handling must target only the self-wrap" rather than as
a runtime promise.

Test seam (r3178622359): the `selfWrapEvent == null` branch in
`sendPrivateMessage` was previously unreachable from the test surface
because `GiftWrapUtil.getGiftWrapEvent` is a static call — synthetic
test keys force the call to throw inside NIP-44 ECDH (covering the
catch path) and real test keys return a non-null event (covering the
success path), but neither setup exercises the in-between case where
the SDK declines to produce an event without throwing.

- New `GiftWrapBuilder` typedef matching the static signature.
- Optional `@visibleForTesting` constructor parameter on
  `NIP17MessageService` defaulting to `GiftWrapUtil.getGiftWrapEvent`,
  threaded through to a private `_giftWrapBuilder` field. Production
  call sites for both the recipient wrap and the self-wrap call go
  through the field, keeping them symmetric — a future test that
  needs to mock the recipient wrap will not require another refactor.
- New test in the "with sender pubkey derived from signer key" group
  injects a builder that delegates to the real `GiftWrapUtil` for the
  first call (so the recipient wrap is a real kind-1059 event flowing
  into the publish path) and returns null on the second call,
  exercising the previously-untested branch and asserting
  `success: true, selfWrapPublished: false`.

Verified: `dart format`, `flutter analyze packages/models
packages/dm_repository lib test integration_test`, the full
`dm_repository` test suite (185 tests passing), and
`conversation_bloc_test.dart` (NIP17SendResult consumer) all clean.

* refactor(dm,models): drop "outgoing queue" forward-refs in tests; add direct builder-throws test

Self-review of #3910's prior commits caught two consistency gaps:

1. The "queue retries / outgoing queue can retry" wording NotThatKindOfDrLiz

* fix(dm): surface NIP-17 self-wrap publish failure via NIP17SendResult

NIP-17 sends two independent gift wraps to relays: one to the recipient
and one to the sender's own pubkey. The self-addressed wrap is what
makes the sender's own messages recoverable on reinstall, second-device
login, or fresh account state — without it, the recipient sees the
message but the sender does not on any other device.

fix(dm): clear optimistic on send failure, surface retry, key bloc on repo identity (#3908)

* fix(dm): clear optimistic on send failure, surface retry, key bloc on repo identity

When an outgoing DM fails (relay reject, slow Keycast RPC, signer error,
DB-persist throw), the ConversationBloc only flipped `sendStatus` to
`failed` and left the optimistic message in `state.messages`. The watch
stream was the sole mechanism that ever removed the optimistic — so on
failure it lingered until the bloc was disposed, then vanished on
re-entry. That reproduces the user's report exactly: "looks sent, then
disappeared when I came back."

Three coordinated changes:

- bloc: strip the optimistic for the failed `pendingId` and record a
  `FailedSend(content, recipientPubkeys)` in state. A new attempt
  clears `lastFailedSend` so the SnackBar can't refire from a stale
  failure.
- view: `BlocListener` on `sendStatus → failed` shows a localized
  SnackBar (`dmSendFailedMessage`) with a Retry action that
  redispatches `ConversationMessageSent` from `lastFailedSend` — UI
  doesn't hold non-UI state.
- page: `BlocProvider<ConversationBloc>` now carries
  `key: ValueKey((dmRepository, currentPubkey))`, mirroring the four
  canonical sites (`video_feed_page.dart`, `pooled_fullscreen_video_
  feed_screen.dart`). Without it, a `dmRepository` captured during a
  brief unauthenticated window scopes all reads/writes by an empty
  `_userPubkey` for the lifetime of the bloc, an independent path to
  the same disappearance symptom.

Tests:
- bloc: pinned `messages: isEmpty` and `lastFailedSend` invariants on
  every failure path; added retry round-trip + state lifecycle tests.
- view: 3 new SnackBar tests (shown on failure, not on success, retry
  redispatches with captured content + recipients).
- page: new `conversation_page_repo_swap_test.dart` mirroring
  `pooled_video_feed_item_repo_swap_test.dart` — recreate-on-flip,
  preserve-on-equal-identity, intentional-state-loss-on-flip.

Closes #3902

* test(l10n): record #3908 dm-send-failure keys in untranslated-debt list

`dmSendFailedMessage` and `dmSendFailedRetry` were added to `app_en.arb`
on this branch without translations. The ARB-consistency test correctly
treats that as drift and fails on the synthetic merge ref.

Adds the two keys to `_knownUntranslatedDebt` with a provenance comment,
matching the established pattern used for every other batch of deferred
translations in this set. Non-English locales fall back to English until
the next translation pass. No app code changes.

* fix(dm): make optimistic pendingId collision-safe (#3908 review)

The failure-cleanup path strips optimistic rows by `m.id != pendingId`,
so the strip's correctness depends on every optimistic row in
`state.messages` having a unique id. The original implementation derived
`pendingId` from a second-resolution timestamp, which collides on rapid
sends — two attempts within the same wall-clock second share an id, and
when the second one fails the cleanup removes both pending rows along
with its own.

Replace the timestamp with a UUID v4 (already in `pubspec.yaml`,
`uuid: ^4.5.1`, used by `BugReportService`). To keep the new contract
testable without depending on real wall-clock timing, expose a
`@visibleForTesting` `pendingIdFactory` constructor parameter that
defaults to a UUID-backed factory.

Adds a regression blocTest that drives two sends through `sequential()`
— the first succeeds (so its optimistic stays in `state.messages`
during the production window where `watchMessages` has not yet emitted
the persisted row), and the second fails. Pins:

  - the second's pending id differs from the first's,
  - the failure cleanup strips only the second's row,
  - the first's optimistic survives in `state.messages`,
  - `lastFailedSend` records only the failing attempt's content.

Under the old timestamp-based id this final state would be `messages:
isEmpty`. Under the new factory it is `messages: [pending-1]`.

Refs: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3908#discussion_r3178612147

* i18n(dm): translate dmSendFailed* across 16 locales (#3908 review)

The previous PR landed `dmSendFailedMessage` and `dmSendFailedRetry`
in `app_en.arb` only and routed every non-English locale through the
`_knownUntranslatedDebt` fallback. Reviewer flagged this as carrying
debt on a primary DM surface: every non-English user would see English
copy on the failure SnackBar and Retry action.

Translates both keys in all 16 non-English locales (am/ar/bg/de/es/fr/
id/it/ja/ko/nl/pl/pt/ro/sv/tr), aligning tone with the existing
locale-specific copy:

- "Retry" matches the locale's existing `commonRetry` / `feedRetry`
  variants (e.g. de "Erneut versuchen", ja "もう一回", nl "Opnieuw").
- "Message couldn't be sent" matches the colloquial register the
  locale already uses for upload-failed copy (e.g. ja "送信できなかった",
  ko "보내지 못했어요", bg "Съобщението не мина").

Regenerates `lib/l10n/generated/app_localizations_*.dart` via
`flutter gen-l10n`. Removes the two debt-list entries from
`arb_consistency_test.dart`; the test now verifies all 16 locales
define both keys.

Refs: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3908#discussion_r3178612148

* a11y(dm): announce send-failure SnackBar via SemanticsService (#3908 review)

`accessibility.md` requires an explicit `SemanticsService.announce` call
on async visible state changes — including when a SnackBar appears.
Material's default SnackBar semantics are platform-dependent and weaker
than the written rule, so reviewer asked for an explicit announce.

Calls `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement` (the non-deprecated form,
mirroring the existing precedent in `feed_auto_advance_cubit.dart`)
right after `messenger.showSnackBar(...)` in `_onSendFailed`. The
announcement uses `Directionality.of(context)` rather than a hardcoded
`TextDirection.ltr` so RTL locales (ar) get the correct reading
direction.

Adds a widget test that intercepts `SystemChannels.accessibility` (the
platform channel both `announce` and `sendAnnouncement` ultimately
deliver through) and pins:

  - the channel receives an `'announce'` event when the SnackBar fires,
  - the announce payload carries the localized failure message,
  - the handler is properly torn down so the test does not leak across
    siblings.

Refs: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3908#discussion_r3178612155

* fix(dm): surface self-wrap publish failure as sentPartial (#3908 review)

Reviewer flagged that `DmRepository.sendMessage()` returned `success: true`
even when the recipient gift wrap landed but the sender's self-addressed
NIP-17 gift wrap silently failed to publish. `_onMessageSent()` only
checked `result.success`, so this branch never surfaced to the UI and
never became retryable — the sender's other devices would not see the
message on relay-only restore, but the conversation would happily flip
to `SendStatus.sent` and the user had no signal anything was wrong.

Folds the missing signal into the send-path contract:

- `NIP17SendResult` gains `selfWrapPublished` (defaults to `true`, set
  explicitly by the success factory). `NIP17MessageService` now checks
  the publish-event return inside its self-wrap try block and reports
  `false` whenever the inner `publishEvent` returned null or threw.
  Existing callers that don't yet track this signal are unaffected.

- `ConversationState` gains `SendStatus.sentPartial`, distinct from
  `sent` (full success) and `failed` (recipient never got it). The bloc
  emits `sentPartial` plus a `lastFailedSend` snapshot when any
  successful per-recipient send had its self-wrap fail (in 1:1 there is
  one; in groups, every-recipient must self-wrap to count as full
  success). The optimistic stays — the message *was* delivered and
  `DmRepository` already persisted it locally — so the UI does not
  flicker between visible and stripped while `watchMessages` catches up.

- `ConversationView` extends the existing `BlocListener` to also fire
  on `sentPartial`, swapping the SnackBar copy to a new localized key
  `dmSendPartialMessage`. Retry reuses `dmSendFailedRetry`. Tapping
  Retry redispatches the full `ConversationMessageSent`, which double-
  delivers to the recipient on success — accepted tradeoff against
  silent loss of cross-device sync, and the principled fix (durable
  outgoing queue with self-wrap-only retry) is tracked in #3909.

Tests:

- `NIP17MessageService`: tightened the existing throws test to also
  pin `selfWrapPublished == false`, and added a returns-null test that
  mirrors the silent-failure shape the reviewer called out.
- `ConversationBloc`: 1:1 partial-delivery test pins the optimistic-
  preserved + `sentPartial` + `lastFailedSend` contract; group test

* fix(dm): make optimistic pendingId collision-safe (#3908 review)

The failure-cleanup path strips optimistic rows by `m.id != pendingId`,

during the production window where `watchMessages` has not yet emitted

commit.message:
fix(clip-manager): treat post-deletion cleanup as best-effort (#4085)

The CI flake on PR #4078 (`fix/top-align-square-videos`, completely
unrelated to ClipManager) caught a latent fragility in
`removeClipById`: after the synchronous state mutation and
forced autosave, the method reads `databaseProvider` and runs
`FileCleanupService.deleteRecordingClipFiles`. Either step can throw
in a test environment that doesn't override `databaseProvider` or
in production if Drift / sqlite has a transient init hiccup, and the
throw rejected the whole future — turning a successful delete into
an apparent failure.

Wrap that tail in try/catch + Log.error so disk-side failures stay
out of the caller's contract. The clip is already gone from state
and the autosave above persists that; cleanup is best-effort.

Add a regression test that pins the contract: `removeClipById`
returns true and leaves state empty even when the test container
provides no database override.
